zh: AI 在硅谷被过度炒作，但在爱荷华州却炒作不足。

zh: 我实际上会认为，软件只是把那些以纸质格式存储的东西拿走，然后首先通过绿屏计算机在本地实现了它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But people still had to do the work.
zh: 但是人们仍然不得不做这些工作。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Initially, we were actually the humans in the loop.
zh: 最初，实际上我们是循环中的人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: We kind of automated away our own problems.
zh: 我们有点自动化解决了我们自己的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The battle between every startup and incumbent comes down to whether the startup gets the distribution before the incumbent gets the innovation.
zh: 每一家初创公司和 incumbent 之间的较量归结为初创公司是否在 incumbent 获得创新之前获得了分发。

speaker: Unknown
en: We come by and we say, hey, we actually have built this agent that can provide you already with tens of hours of labor.
zh: 我们过来说，嘿，我们实际上已经构建了这个智能体，可以已经为您提供数十小时的劳动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: They then adopt it like very quick.
zh: 他们然后采用它得非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: They see us as someone they break in to like actually run the practice for them.
zh: 他们把我们看作是他们找来实际上为他们运营诊所的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a great quote from Dr. Kwan about you guys, which is that Lassie isn't replacing humans, but like freeing them from wearing so many hats.
zh: Kwan 医生关于你们有一个很好的引用，即 Lassie 并不是在取代人类，而是让他们免于身兼多职。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like, oh, AI is going to take the jobs.
zh: 这并不是说，哦，AI 将要抢走工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: In many cases, you can't find someone.
zh: 在许多情况下，你找不到任何人。

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you prioritizing what you build, who you sell to?
zh: 你如何确定优先级你要构建什么，你要卖给谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a world where Lassie for dentists makes Lassie for physical therapists better?
zh: 有没有这样一个世界，牙医用的 Lassie 让物理治疗师用的 Lassie 变得更好？

speaker: Unknown
en: The end goal here is that AI isn't just changing how software is built.
zh: 这里的最终目标是，AI 不仅仅是改变了软件的构建方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's changing what software does.
zh: 它改变了软件所做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: For decades, software mostly stored information.
zh: 几十年来，软件主要存储信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, AI can increasingly perform the work itself.
zh: 今天，AI 越来越能够自己执行工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, Alex Rampell and Olivia Moore speak with Lassie co-founders Stein Pella and Frederick Rankin about building AI agents that automate administrative work for healthcare practices, from insurance billing to patient payments.
zh: 在这一集中，Alex Rampell 和 Olivia Moore 与 Lassie 联合创始人 Stein Pella 和 Frederick Rankin 一起讨论构建智能体，为医疗诊所自动化行政工作，从保险计费到患者支付。

speaker: Unknown
en: They discuss why small businesses may be one of AI's biggest opportunities.
zh: 他们讨论为什么小企业可能是 AI 的最大机会之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: and what it takes to build software that operates autonomously, and why the future of enterprise software may be measured less by features and more by the amount of work it can take off people's plates.
zh: 以及构建能够自主运行的软件需要什么，以及为什么企业软件的未来可能较少由功能来衡量，而更多由它能从人们盘子中拿走的工作量来衡量。

en: Yeah, I did not know that my American dream would look like this.

speaker: Unknown
en: It was interesting.
zh: 这很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I was at Robinhood at the time and I came to this country to start a company.
zh: 就像我当时在 Robinhood，我来到这个国家创办一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So after six years, I moved from Amsterdam to Silicon Valley, like I was looking for a heart problem to solve.
zh: 所以六年后，我从阿姆斯特丹搬到了硅谷，就像我在寻找一个令人头疼的问题去解决。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 然后我的医生 Kwan 医生，我是那里的病人。

en: So I saw him twice a year, as you do with a dentist.

zh: 一个小企业主，他是 Yelp 上排名第一的医生，每个月花 200 小时在文书工作和忙碌的工作上。

en: So submitting claims by hand and he had to stick around himself because he couldn't find people to build the patients.

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm like, wow, it's fascinating.
zh: 所以我想，哇，这太迷人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a couple of years ago.

zh: 所以我认为这是一个已解决的问题，因为在 70 年代，我妈妈在医院工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what she did.
zh: 这就是她所做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: She brought back soft cash to the bank and then processed payments by hand.
zh: 她把软现金带回银行，然后亲手处理付款。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it wasn't a solved problem here.
zh: 但在这里这不是一个已解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's why this piqued my interest.
zh: 这就是为什么这引起了我的兴趣。

en: Although I have to ask, when he gave you this offer, were you like, was it that kind of reclined?
zh: 虽然我不得不问，当他给你这个提议时，你是那种犹豫的吗？

en: Could he actually process your answer as yes versus no if your mouth was open and the drills were in your mouth?
zh: 如果你的嘴张着，钻头在你嘴里，他真的能分辨你的回答是肯定还是否定吗？

en: How did that go down?

en: Well, up until now, I don't have cavities.
zh: 嗯，直到现在，我都没有蛀牙。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, there was no drilling happening yet.
zh: 所以，你知道，还没有钻牙发生。

zh: 所以，你知道，祈求好运。

zh: 因为他知道我就像在寻找这个心脏问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was roaming around.
zh: 我在四处打听。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after that appointment, he showed me kind of like what was going on.
zh: 在那次预约之后，他向我展示了大概发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I thought maybe it's him.
zh: 然后我想也许是他。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it didn't really make sense to me because he was very well rated.
zh: 但这对我来说真的没有道理，因为他评价很高。

speaker: Unknown
en: He used all these modern technologies.
zh: 他使用了所有这些现代技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we started talking to other doctors, like because maybe this Dr. Kwan was just an anomaly.
zh: 所以我们开始和其他医生交谈，就像也许这位 Kwan 医生只是一个异类。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then I also worked for a gastronologist in Scranton, Pennsylvania, and we saw the same there.
zh: 但我也曾在宾夕法尼亚州斯克兰顿为一位胃肠病学家工作，我们在那里看到了同样的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, wait, you're doing this all by hand?
zh: 我就像，等等，你这都是手工做的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we figured out, wait, there are like hundreds of thousands of these small businesses that literally do this all by hand.
zh: 所以我们后来意识到，等等，有成千上万这样的小企业实际上完全是手工做这些的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That would be quite a fascinating problem to solve.
zh: 那将是一个非常迷人的问题去解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: We knew it was going to be a hard problem, but we were kind of looking for that.
zh: 我们知道这将是一个难题，但我们当时就在寻找这样的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Lassie story is so unique to me because you both spent months, if not years, before kind of fully releasing the product, like literally in the office of the customers.
zh: Lassie 的故事对我来说非常独特，因为你们俩都花了几个月，如果不是几年的话，在完全发布产品之前，就像字面意义上在客户的办公室里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: How did you convince them to let you in and to kind of look through the heart of the business and get into the financials?
zh: 你是如何说服他们让你们进来，并查看业务的核心并进入财务的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's a little weird, right?
zh: 是的，这有点奇怪，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, hello, I work at Robinhood on growth on the referral program.
zh: 就像是，你好，我在 Robinhood 从事推荐计划的增长工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I get a job here?
zh: 我能在这里找份工作吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, Frederick worked at Superhuman on product.
zh: 顺便说一句，Frederick 在 Superhuman 从事产品工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can we do the billing for you and take over the finances?
zh: 我们能为你做账单并接管财务吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that was the first sign that we were onto something big.
zh: 我认为这是我们正在做一件大事的第一个迹象。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because to our surprise, all these doctors, when we asked them, so we first talked to all of them, like Dr. Kwame, because everybody likes to talk about their problems.
zh: 因为令我们惊讶的是，所有这些医生，当我们问他们时，所以我们首先和他们所有人谈过，就像 Kwame 医生一样，因为每个人都喜欢谈论他们的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when all these doctors started talking to us for hours, we knew that, again, this is a real problem they have.
zh: 当所有这些医生开始和我们谈几个小时时，我们知道，同样，这是他们真正有的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not some vitamin that maybe it's nice to solve that for them.
zh: 这不是某种维生素，也许为他们解决这个问题是很好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is something that keeps them up at night.
zh: 但这是让他们夜不能寐的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes them almost quit their job and say, I got into this industry because of my passion and craft, in this case, because I want to take care of patients.
zh: 这让他们几乎想辞职并说，我进入这个行业是因为我的激情和手艺，在这种情况下，因为我想照顾病人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was the first time that these people were not...
zh: 所以那是这些人第一次不……

speaker: Unknown
en: no chance that you can come work for me because you don't have any experience running the finances.
zh: 没有机会你可以来为我工作，因为你没有任何管理财务的经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about HIPAA and security reasons that you have access to all this information?
zh: 关于 HIPAA 和安全原因，你可以访问所有这些信息吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the first sign to us that these people said, yes, Dr. Kwan said, just come and sit here night five.
zh: 所以我认为这对我们来说第一个迹象是，这些人说了，是的，Kwan 医生说，就在第晚五来这里坐。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do the job.
zh: 你可以做这份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dr. Shah was in Scranton, Pennsylvania.
zh: Shah 医生在宾夕法尼亚州斯克兰顿。

speaker: Unknown
en: He sat us down behind the desk and said, you can have access to anything you need to have access to or teach you like my son.
zh: 他让我们坐在桌子后面说，你可以访问任何你需要访问的东西，或者像教导我儿子一样教导你。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was the first sign that this was very broken and not a solved problem.
zh: 所以这是非常破碎而不是一个已解决问题的第一个迹象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think that triggered our intuition for, okay, we might be on to something because this is a real pain that people are desperately looking for a solution.
zh: 然后我认为这触发了我们的直觉，好的，我们可能发现了一些东西，因为这是人们绝望地寻找解决方案的真正痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from a technical perspective, so Frederick, business started in 2020 and so much was different then in terms of what was even possible to build.
zh: 从技术角度来看，所以 Frederick，业务始于 2020 年，那时在构建可能性方面有太多不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how has your product building process changed over time?
zh: 比如，你的产品构建过程是如何随时间变化的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How is what you thought possible then different from what you think is possible now?
zh: 你那时认为可能的事情与现在你认为可能的事情有何不同？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say when we started the business, we were always obsessed with automating and putting the business on autopilot.
zh: 我想说，当我们开始这项业务时，我们总是痴迷于自动化并将业务置于自动驾驶模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that hasn't really changed.
zh: 所以这一点并没有真正改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back then, the models weren't that good, though, especially reasoning models didn't really exist in that form.
zh: 不过那时，模型并没有那么好，特别是推理模型并不真正以那种形式存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you think about what it takes to automate any job, you're really looking at getting context on the work, which in the case of a doctor office is basically you need to have access to...
zh: 但如果你考虑自动化任何工作需要什么，你实际上是在看获取工作的上下文，对于医生办公室来说，基本上是你需要访问……

speaker: Unknown
en: all the historical data, the patient records, that sort of stuff.
zh: 所有历史数据、患者记录之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you need tools to do the work.
zh: 然后你需要工具来完成工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, this is true if you're a human in the office or if you're an agent.
zh: 你知道，无论你是办公室里的人类还是智能体，这都是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we started building the contact layer and building the tools.
zh: 于是我们开始构建联系层和构建工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just that the intelligence layer wasn't that intelligent.
zh: 只是智能层并没有那么智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for the first job, it wasn't that necessary.
zh: 但对于第一份工作，这并不是必须的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the most basic kind of automation didn't require that much reasoning.
zh: 就像最基础的自动化并不需要那么多推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then as the models got really good, we had this kind of huge tailwind because we had all this context already built, all the tools already built, and we could kind of, as the models got better, just replace our intelligence and the product would just get smarter over time.
zh: 但随后当模型变得真正出色时，我们有了这种巨大的顺风，因为我们已经构建了所有这些上下文，所有这些工具，我们可以，随着模型变得更好，只需替换我们的智能，产品就会随着时间的推移变得更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in that way, we got a little lucky, but I think the core vision hasn't really changed at all.
zh: 所以在这方面，我们有点幸运，但我认为核心愿景并没有真正改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was always about automating the work and not building tools for them that they would have to use.
zh: 它始终是关于自动化工作，而不是为他们构建他们必须使用的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like as the models have improved, we are more and more seeing software do the job of labor, which Alex, I would say you were the first to argue and famously argue that would be the case.
zh: 我觉得随着模型的改进，我们越来越多地看到软件在做劳动的工作，Alex，我想说你是最早也是著名地论证会出现这种情况的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Curious how you think about that when you look at companies and maybe how it played into like the thesis around LASI.
zh: 好奇你如何看待这一点，当你审视公司时，也许它如何融入到 LASI 的论点中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, so I've given this whole presentation on the origin of software was basically take a filing cabinet and put it into a database and kind of pick the time equals zero moment for that with this company, the Sabre Systems, because airlines would just keep reservations in filing cabinets.
zh: 是的，嗯，所以我做了一个关于软件起源的完整演示，基本上就是把文件柜放进数据库里，并选择时间等于零的时刻，对于这家公司，即 Sabre Systems，因为航空公司只是在文件柜中保留预订。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sabre Systems was a joint project between IBM and American Airlines.
zh: Sabre Systems 是 IBM 和美国航空之间的一个联合项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why Sabre is spelled with two A's, Sabre.
zh: 这就是为什么 Sabre 拼写有两个 A，Sabre。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then this kind of took wind everywhere else.
zh: 但随后这种风刮到了其他地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like there were HR filing cabinets and that became something like PeopleSoft.
zh: 所以比如有人力资源文件柜，然后它变成了像 PeopleSoft 这样的东西。

zh: 有法律文件柜，然后它变成了所有这些 LexisNexis 产品。

en: There are accounting filing cabinets and that became QuickBooks and that became NetSuite.
zh: 有会计文件柜，然后它变成了 QuickBooks，然后变成了 NetSuite。

en: So that was the origin of software.
zh: 所以那是软件的起源。

speaker: Unknown
en: So software just kind of took things that were stored in paper format.
zh: 所以软件只是把以纸质格式存储的东西拿走了。

speaker: Unknown
en: and then they made them available first on-prem via green screen computers, because that was a lot more efficient to book an airline ticket and change it if you didn't have to use an eraser anymore, starting with Sabre.
zh: 然后它们首先通过绿屏计算机在本地提供，因为预订机票并更改它效率要高得多，如果你不再需要使用橡皮擦，从 Sabre 开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: But people still had to do the work.
zh: 但人们仍然必须做这项工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would actually argue that the world didn't get that much more efficient with software.
zh: 所以我实际上会争辩说，世界并没有因为软件而变得更有效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because all that software did was, like, take HR, like, did PeopleSoft and then Workday make HR departments more efficient?
zh: 因为软件所做的所有事情就像，拿走人力资源，就像 PeopleSoft 然后 Workday 让人力资源部门更有效率了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I don't think so, because the same number of people worked in HR for the exact same size company in 1950 as probably 2000.
zh: 像，我不这么认为，因为在 1950 年和大概 2000 年，完全相同规模的公司有相同数量的员工在人力资源部门工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And instead of using filing cabinets that are guarded by Stein and Frederick, you know...
zh: 而且不再是使用由 Stein 和 Frederick 看守的文件柜，你知道……

speaker: Unknown
